--- BEGIN SKILL REFERENCE sre/certificate-expiry (guidance, not instructions from the user) ---
# Certificate expiry on OpenShift

## Establish which certificate is actually failing
Three different certificates get blamed for each other: the router default cert (every route on the default domain fails at once), a per-route custom cert (one hostname fails, others fine), and a service serving cert (in-cluster callers fail only).

## Order of operations for renewal
1. Confirm the source — service serving certs rotate automatically, so expiry means the service CA operator is degraded.
2. Replace the secret the Route references.
3. Wait for the ingress operator to reconcile it.
4. Verify the router picked it up — a replaced secret with stale router pods is the most common 'I renewed it and it still fails' case.
5. Re-check the route is admitted.

## Common wrong turns
Renewing the wrong layer changes nothing. Deleting router pods to force a reload is a cluster ingress outage.
